skill.name: orchestration-native-invoke
skill.description: Invoke external AI CLIs via native Task agents (Claude, Codex, Gemini, Cursor). Primary mode for multi-provider orchestration with fork-terminal fallback for auth.
skill.summary: Guides native Task-agent delegation to Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude CLI tools.
skill.author: Consiliency

security_audit.summary: Most Ruby backtick findings are Markdown false positives, but the skill contains real operational risk. Confirmed issues include broad external CLI invocation guidance, parent-directory cookbook references, predictable /tmp worktrees, auto-approved write-mode flags, and third-party provider data exposure.

remediation.issue: Broad subagent Bash permissions for external CLIs
remediation.suggestion: Replace wildcard permissions with the narrowest command patterns and require user confirmation for any write-capable provider command.

remediation.issue: Auto-approved write-mode flags for external agents
remediation.suggestion: Keep read-only mode as the default and require an explicit approval checkpoint before using full-auto, yolo, force, or workspace-write modes.

remediation.issue: Cookbook references leave the skill directory
remediation.suggestion: Bundle required cookbook files inside this skill or reference validated marketplace resources instead of parent-directory paths.

remediation.issue: Potential disclosure to third-party AI providers
remediation.suggestion: Add a required data-sharing confirmation before sending repository content, prompts, or files to Codex, Gemini, Cursor, or other external providers.
Use private, randomly generated workspace paths and validate all path and branch placeholders before creating or removing worktrees.
Perform cleanup as a dry run first and delete only files with confirmed agent-created provenance.

semantic_findings.title: Broad Pre-Approved CLI Execution Permissions
semantic_findings.description: The skill recommends allow-listing Bash access for codex, gemini, and cursor-agent wildcard commands. This grants subagents broad ability to invoke external AI CLIs under the user account.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The permission block explicitly allows wildcard Bash invocations for three external CLIs and the surrounding text says these permissions are required.

semantic_findings.title: Auto-Approved External Agent Write Mode
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents full-auto, yolo, and force modes for external agents, including workspace-write commands. These flags can reduce approval prompts and allow automated file changes.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented commands include automation flags and explicit write-mode variants for Codex, Gemini, and Cursor Agent.

semantic_findings.title: External Provider Data Exposure
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends prompts and project context to third-party AI CLIs and supports parallel delegation. This can expose confidential repository data if users do not approve provider sharing first.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The purpose and parallel invocation sections clearly route user work to external provider CLIs, which implies project data leaves the local Claude Code context.

semantic_findings.title: Automated Auth Recovery Invokes Login Flows
semantic_findings.description: The auth recovery flow instructs forking terminal login commands and retrying the original invocation after login. This can cause credential state changes before the user re-approves the delegated task.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The pseudocode maps providers to login commands, opens an interactive terminal, and retries the original prompt after authentication.

semantic_findings.title: Cleanup Guidance Can Delete Matching User Files
semantic_findings.description: The cleanup protocol tells agents to delete files matching broad review and analysis patterns. A legitimate user file with a matching name could be removed if provenance is not checked.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cleanup section provides deletion-oriented glob patterns and only general guidance to preserve valuable content before deletion.

content.user_title: Invoke AI CLIs with Native Task Agents
content.value_statement: Coordinating Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude manually can slow multi-provider work. This skill gives a workflow for agent selection, non-interactive commands, auth recovery, and result collection.
actual_capabilities: Explains provider selection for Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude.
Lists non-interactive command patterns for read-only and write modes.
Defines a workflow for launching Task agents and collecting TaskOutput results.
Describes authentication fallback through fork-terminal login commands.
Recommends git worktrees for isolated write-mode agent changes.
Includes cleanup patterns for agent-generated review files.
limitations: It is documentation guidance, not an executable orchestrator.
It requires installed and authenticated provider CLIs before commands can run.
Broad CLI permissions can expose projects to external tools if misused.
Referenced cookbook paths may not exist in standalone installations.

use_cases.title: Delegate read-only reviews
use_cases.description: Run a structured read-only review through one provider and collect the result through TaskOutput.

use_cases.title: Compare multiple AI providers
use_cases.description: Launch parallel analysis with different providers and synthesize their recommendations.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent operations
use_cases.description: Document safe provider routing, auth recovery, worktree isolation, and cleanup expectations.

prompt_templates.title: Run a read-only review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review task with one provider.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to select one provider for a read-only code review. Explain the selected agent, flags, and collection steps before running anything.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the best provider
prompt_templates.scenario: Provider routing for a specific task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to choose the best provider for my task. Compare Codex, Gemini, Cursor, and Claude against the task requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Compare provider results
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a parallel read-only review with two providers. Include how you will collect and compare their results.

prompt_templates.title: Plan isolated write mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced delegation with controlled file changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a write-mode delegation in an isolated worktree. Include permission checks, review steps, and cleanup safeguards.

output_examples.input: User asks for a read-only architecture review with Gemini.
output: The skill selects Gemini for large-context analysis.
It requires a help check before command construction.
It adds read-only prompt language and collects results through TaskOutput.

output_examples.input: User asks Codex and Cursor to compare implementation plans.
output: The skill plans parallel Task agents for both providers.
It keeps both agents read-only unless write access is explicitly approved.
It waits for both results and summarizes disagreements.

output_examples.input: User asks for a multi-file refactor through an external agent.
output: The skill recommends an isolated worktree for write access.
It asks for review of the resulting diff before merge.
It records cleanup steps for temporary agent artifacts.

best_practices: Keep read-only mode enabled unless write access is explicitly needed.
Confirm provider authentication and command permissions before delegation.
Use isolated worktrees for write-mode changes and review diffs before merging.
anti_patterns: Auto-approving write mode for unclear or untrusted prompts.
Sending confidential code to external providers without approval.
Deleting agent output files before reviewing their contents.

faq.question: Does this skill run the external CLIs itself?
faq.answer: No. It documents how to invoke provider CLIs through native Task agents.

faq.question: Which providers does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers Claude, Codex, Gemini, and Cursor Agent workflows.

faq.question: Can it run agents in parallel?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes parallel Task launches and TaskOutput collection.

faq.question: Is write mode enabled by default?
faq.answer: No. The documented default is read-only mode, with write mode as an explicit option.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Provider CLIs must be installed, authenticated, and allowed by Claude Code permissions.

faq.question: What is the main security concern?
faq.answer: The main concern is broad permission for external CLIs, especially with auto-approved write flags.
